The residual axiom asserts normalized revised/original text projection equalities for this repo's inplace atomizer output.
Lean normalizeText models trim plus blank-entry dropping, not every TypeScript regex behavior.
Lean extractText keeps structural order; TypeScript extractTextWithParagraphs has known ordering differences outside the compared surfaces.

The text projection counts w:t, w:delText and w:sym (resolved to its @w:char codepoint). It does not count w:br, w:tab, w:cr, w:noBreakHyphen, w:softHyphen, w:pgNum, w:drawing, w:pict or w:object, and normalizeText erases leading/trailing whitespace and blank paragraph entries, so losing any of those leaves the invariant satisfied.
Lean atomText models w:t and w:delText only; the TypeScript projection additionally counts w:sym, so the Lean model under-approximates the shipped projection on symbol-bearing documents.

invariants.statement: For every fixed WordprocessingML story accepted by the compiled checker, tracked move ranges have unique typed decimal ids, non-empty names, balanced non-crossing endpoints, exactly one range per direction and move name, and matching source/destination move names.
caveats: MoveRangesWellFormed is witnessed by an inductive trace whose starts require fresh Int ids and fresh non-empty directional names, whose ends pop the exact same-direction id, and whose final state has an empty stack and matching source/destination name membership.

Both Strict and Transitional schemas type move range ids as ST_DecimalNumber restricted from xsd:integer. Numeric aliases canonicalize to Int and malformed ids reject. Required ST_String names can be empty at schema level; the checker deliberately imposes a stronger non-empty identity rule.

The executable strictly decodes package parts as UTF-8, accepts one leading UTF-8 BOM, and permits only absent or case-insensitive UTF-8 declaration encoding. The parser accepts one namespace-qualified XML root and whitespace outside it, validates XML 1.0 characters/references in every element namespace, applies XML attribute-value normalization before resolving references, rejects duplicate ordinary attributes by expanded name, validates QNames, and rejects comments, other processing instructions, DTDs, and CDATA rather than treating them as checked content.
This is a per-document checker guarantee over the fixed main, footnote, and endnote stories, not a universal proof of every safe-docx emission path.
The checker pairs source and destination range identities by w:name but does not associate individual w:moveFrom or w:moveTo revision ids with a range id.
The public certificate remains limited to inplace reconstruction output.
